message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical, Chemical, and Isotopic Properties** | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic number** | 1 | | **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average; dominated by the most abundant isotope, protium) | | **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | | **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | | **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) | | **Molecular form** | H₂ (diatomic) under normal conditions | | **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | | **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | | **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.00008988 g cm⁻³) | | **Color** | Colorless | | **Odor** | Odorless | | **Taste** | Tasteless | | **State at room temperature** | Gas | | **Solubility in water** | ~1.6 g L⁻¹ (≈0.018 mol L⁻¹) | | **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (range 4–75 % by volume) | | **Reactivity** | Forms hydrides with metals; reacts with halogens, oxygen, and many other elements under appropriate conditions | | **Isotopes** | • **Protium** (¹H, 99.98 %) – single proton, no neutrons.
• **Deuterium** (²H or D, 0.02 %) – one proton, one neutron.
• **Tritium** (³H or T, trace) – one proton, two neutrons; radioactive (β⁻ decay, half‑life ≈12.32 y). | | **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds (e.g., H₂, H₂O, CH₄). In ionic form, it can act as a proton (H⁺) in acids. | | **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – key in astrophysics. | | **Applications** | • Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells).
• Chemical industry (ammonia synthesis, methanol, hydrogenation).
• Space propulsion (liquid hydrogen as rocket propellant).
• Medical imaging (tritium labeling).
• Research (ultra‑cold hydrogen, quantum fluids). | | **Safety notes** | • Extremely flammable; requires careful handling.
• Tritium is radioactive; must be contained and monitored.
• Hydrogen embrittlement can weaken metals. | ### Quick Summary - **Physical**: Lightest element, colorless, odorless, tasteless gas at room temperature; very low density and boiling/melting points. - **Chemical**: Highly reactive; forms diatomic molecules (H₂) and a wide range of compounds; acts as a proton donor in acids. - **Isotopic**: Exists mainly as protium, with trace deuterium and tritium; isotopic differences affect mass, nuclear properties, and reactivity. - **Practical**: Central to energy technologies (fuel cells, rockets), industrial chemistry, and scientific research. Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
